title: Visual polish: fonts, color-coded options, animations
description: The current UI uses Ebitengine's DebugPrintAt for all text, which renders in a small monospace debug font. This was fine for prototyping but looks rough for a playable game. Improvements needed: (1) Proper font rendering — use Ebitengine's text/v2 package with an embedded TTF font for chord names, labels, and UI text. (2) Color-code chord options by harmonic category rather than by index — e.g. green for resolutions (V->I, bII7->I), blue for diatonic movement (circle of 5ths), purple for chromatic/borrowed chords (tritone subs, modal interchange), gold for secondary dominants. The transition graph already has weight data that loosely correlates with these categories, but a category field on Transition would be cleaner. (3) Smoother animations — bar scrolling is linear, could benefit from subtle easing; selection feedback beyond the current hover overlay; pulse/glow on the pending bar as it approaches the bar line. Consult with James on font choice and specific color scheme preferences.

title: Design and document the rhythm game mechanics
description: Design/spec session for the guitar-hero style game. Produces a markdown design doc covering: lane layout, input mapping, game flow (start/play/score), timing model, scoring model, audio strategy, difficulty. DoD: design doc committed to repo, detailed enough to derive implementation beads from it.

title: Add audio: piano chord playback and basic beat
description: Add audio feedback to the chord composition game using Web Audio API synthesis (no audio files needed). Piano chords: map each chord symbol to constituent note frequencies, trigger multiple oscillators with ADSR envelopes for piano-like tones. Auto-voicing layer should pick octaves/inversions for smooth voice leading between chords. Basic beat: simple kick/hihat pattern synced to the BPM to give rhythmic context. Consult with James on: preferred instrument sound (piano vs organ vs other), whether the beat should be optional/toggleable, volume controls, and how prominent the audio should be relative to the decision-making gameplay.

title: Genre switching: swap transition graphs for pop/blues
description: The chord composition game was architecturally designed so that the transition graph is the only thing that changes per genre. The current implementation has a single jazz graph (ii-V-I, tritone subs, secondary dominants, modal interchange, etc.) defined in chords.go as transitionGraph. To support other genres: (1) Pop graph — I-V-vi-IV patterns, simpler diatonic movement, fewer chromatic options. (2) Blues graph — I7-IV7-V7 with chromatic passing chords, shuffle feel. Each genre would be a separate map[ChordFunction][]Transition. The game would need a genre selector on the title screen. The ChordFunction enum may need extending for genre-specific chords (e.g. dominant 7th on every degree for blues). Consult with James on which genres to prioritize and whether genre should be changeable mid-song or only at start.

title: Sub-bar chord changes: two chords per bar
description: Currently the game operates at one chord per bar. For faster harmonic rhythm (common in jazz), support two chord changes per bar — e.g. Dm7 for beats 1-2, G7 for beats 3-4. This was identified in the original design spec as a later enhancement. Implementation: the bar visual would split into two halves, each with its own chord slot. The scrolling/timing system already tracks fractional bar positions (scrollX), so the decision points would trigger at half-bar boundaries as well as full-bar boundaries. The transition graph works the same — each half-bar chord resolves to the next using the same rules. This could be toggled as a difficulty setting (1 chord/bar = easy, 2 chords/bar = advanced). Consult with James on whether this should be a toggle or a progressive difficulty increase, and whether the visual split should be explicit (two boxes) or subtle (a divider within one bar).

title: Modulation support: key changes mid-song
description: Implement key modulation in the chord composition game. Certain chord choices can function in multiple keys (pivot chords) — when the player selects one, the game should offer transition options in both the original and potential new keys. Implementation: extend the transition graph to detect pivot chords, update the key display when modulation occurs, and limit modulation targets to common destinations (relative minor/major, dominant key, up a half-step) to avoid overwhelming the player. Consult with James on: which modulation targets to support, how to visually indicate a key change, and whether modulation should be automatic or player-confirmed.

title: Set up Go + Ebitengine WASM scaffold on /game route
description: Set up the foundational plumbing so a Go + Ebitengine game compiles to WASM and renders in the browser on a new /game route. Includes: game/ Go module, Ebitengine dependency, hello-world main.go, wasm_exec.js, build script, React Router integration, and GamePage.tsx component that loads the WASM. DoD: /game renders the Ebitengine hello-world screen; existing site unaffected.
